title: Complete metric abelian groups are reconstructed from shrinking open-subgroup quotients
statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group with a complete translation-invariant metric $d$, so $d(x+z,y+z)=d(x,y)$ and every Cauchy sequence converges, and assume addition and negation are continuous. Let $(U_n)_{n\geq1}$ be additive subgroups, open for the metric topology, with $U_{n+1}\subseteq U_n$. Suppose that for every real $\epsilon>0$ there is $N\geq1$ such that $d(u,0)<\epsilon$ for all $u\in U_N$. Give $G/U_n$ the discrete topology, let $q_n:G\to G/U_n$ be the quotient homomorphism, and let $t_n:G/U_{n+1}\to G/U_n$ be the quotient transition. Put
$$H=\{(a_n)\in\prod_{n\geq1}G/U_n:t_n(a_{n+1})=a_n\text{ for all }n\},$$
with coordinatewise addition and the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology] of the product. Then $q:G\to H$, $x\mapsto(q_n(x))_n$, is an isomorphism of groups and a homeomorphism. For every topological space $S$, writing $C(S,D)$ for continuous maps with pointwise group operations, the quotient maps induce a group isomorphism
$$C(S,G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{(a_n)\in\prod_{n\geq1}C(S,G/U_n):t_n\circ a_{n+1}=a_n\text{ for all }n\}.$$
These isomorphisms commute with precomposition by every continuous map $S'\to S$ and with the displayed quotient projections. Neither compactness of $G$ nor finiteness of $G/U_n$ is assumed.

proof.text: Each $t_n$ is a homomorphism, so the compatibility equations defining $H$ are preserved by addition, zero and negation. Thus $H$ is a subgroup of the product. Since $t_nq_{n+1}=q_n$, the map $q$ takes values in $H$, and $q(x+y)=q(x)+q(y)$ holds coordinatewise.

proof.text: If $q(x)=q(y)$, then $x-y\in U_n$ for every $n$. Given $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ by shrinking. Translation invariance gives $d(x,y)=d(x-y,0)<\epsilon$. If $x\ne y$, choosing $\epsilon=d(x,y)>0$ contradicts this strict inequality. Hence $q$ is injective.

proof.text: Fix $a=(a_n)\in H$ and choose representatives $x_n\in G$ with $q_n(x_n)=a_n$. For $m\ge n$ one has $q_n(x_m)=a_n$: this holds for $m=n$; the induction step composes the quotient map $G/U_{m+1}\to G/U_m$ with $G/U_m\to G/U_n$ and uses $t_m(a_{m+1})=a_m$. Consequently $x_m-x_n\in U_n$.

proof.text: For $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ with $d(u,0)<\epsilon$ on $U_N$. For $m,k\ge N$, step 3 gives $x_m-x_N,x_k-x_N\in U_N$, hence $x_m-x_k\in U_N$ and $d(x_m,x_k)<\epsilon$. This is precisely the Cauchy condition. The completeness assumed in the statement supplies $x\in G$ with $x_m\to x$.

proof.text: Fix n. The quotient projection q_n is continuous for the quotient topology, and G/U_n is discrete because U_n is open, hence Hausdorff. By step 3 the sequence q_n(x_m) is eventually the constant a_n. If x_m tends to x by step 4, continuity gives q_n(x_m) tending to q_n(x). Uniqueness of a limit in this discrete quotient gives q_n(x)=a_n. Thus x realizes all coordinates, proving surjectivity; step 2 proves independence of representatives.

proof.text: Mathlib quotient projections are continuous. Their product q is continuous coordinatewise, and its factorization through H is continuous for the subtype topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Together with steps 2 and 5 this gives an additive equivalence e_0 whose forward map is continuous.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), proof, printed p. 59: continuous-function inverse-limit identity; agent-written general metric-group argument, expanded from coord/reports/Q120/lem-sfb-complete-norm-open-test.md, Source readings and retained argument.

proof.text: Write $h=q^{-1}$ for the bijective inverse. Fix $a=q(x)\in H$ and $\epsilon>0$, and choose $N$ by shrinking. The cylinder $W=\{b\in H:b_N=a_N\}$ is open in the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology] and contains $a$. If $b\in W$, then $h(b)-x\in U_N$, so $d(h(b),x)<\epsilon$. Thus $h$ is continuous at every $a$. Together with the preceding steps this proves that $q$ is a homeomorphism and a group isomorphism.

proof.text: For any topological space S, send f to its continuous quotient-coordinate maps. Conversely, a compatible family (a_n) defines the map A(s)=(a_n(s)) into H, continuous by coordinatewise continuity and the subtype topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. The map e_0 inverse composed with A is continuous by step 7. The coordinate equations for e_0 and its two inverse identities show that these assignments are mutually inverse, also for the empty space.

proof.text: Pointwise sums and negatives of continuous maps to $G$ are continuous by the assumed continuity of addition and negation: locally choose neighborhoods of the two values whose sums lie in a prescribed open, and intersect their inverse images. The discrete quotients have the same property. For all $s\in S$, $q_n(f(s)+g(s))=q_n(f(s))+q_n(g(s))$, so the bijection in step 8 is a group isomorphism. If $v:S\prime\to S$ is continuous, $q_n\circ(f\circ v)=(q_n\circ f)\circ v$; these identities give precomposition naturality and the required quotient-projection compatibility, also for the inverse by uniqueness.
